statement: A runtime_service REPLACE persists and starts exactly one canonical entityId-rN target, proves that target authoritatively ACTIVE before retiring the source, preserves the proof across restart and replay, and leaves no opaque replace-replica runtime, duplicate ADD, endpoint, query slot, or execution loop; partition and message-group REPLACE behavior remains unchanged.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Before changing production code, prove the defect through the production coordinator, durable operation, runtime handler, lifecycle, SERVICES publication, source retirement, and next placement evaluation. The discriminator must be red on current HEAD for the invisible target and duplicate-effect chain and red on reverting the fix.

Keep deterministic replace-op-* operation identity for cross-coordinator dedupe, but runtime_service targets must be durably claimed canonical entityId-rN identities before dispatch. Partition and message-group deterministic REPLACE target behavior remains unchanged.

Canonical runtime target allocation is owned by an authoritative durable single-winner claim. Local mutexes, observational max-plus-one reads, and storage reservations are not sufficient. Same-intent losers adopt the persisted winner; distinct-intent collisions defer or reallocate through a bounded owner retry.

Do not widen runtime-service entity membership or request-routing classifiers to accept replace-replica-* identities. Dispatched creates require strict entityId-rN identity before executable side effects.

RUNTIME_SERVICE_CREATE_ACTIVE is reconciliation evidence, not permission to retire the source. Source retirement and terminalization require a strict canonical target identity and authoritative target-ACTIVE evidence on the intended node; missing or stale evidence defers through one bounded retry owner.

Restart and replay reconstruct the persisted target claim and converge once. Persisted or running legacy replace-replica-* runtime targets are never aliased or abandoned: the lifecycle owner establishes canonical coverage before stopping the invalid target, including when the original operation is already terminal.

The named scenario must force one runtime_service REPLACE through the real owner seam and prove canonical first start, target-ACTIVE handoff, source retirement, terminal operation, stable desired count, and one endpoint, query slot, and execution effect. Opportunistic non-engagement is not a pass.

The unchanged MovieLens scenario remains corroboration only when runtime_service REPLACE actually engages. Do not weaken its identity, freshness, boundedness, placement, or exact-result checks, and do not repeat runs merely to sample engagement.
